title: TIME Data Type
description: Learn how to use the TIME data type to store time values in SQL Server.

data.text: The TIME data type defines a time of a day based on a 24-hour clock. It stores only the time component without a date.

data.title: TIME Syntax
data.content: Defines a TIME column with optional fractional seconds precision.

data.text: The fractional second scale ranges from 0 to 7. The default is 7 if not specified. A TIME value with default precision requires 5 bytes of storage.

data.title: Create TIME Columns
data.content: Creates a table with TIME columns for visit start and end times.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE sales.visits (
    visit_id INT PRIMARY KEY IDENTITY,
    customer_name VARCHAR (50) NOT NULL,
    phone VARCHAR (25),
    store_id INT NOT NULL,
    visit_on DATE NOT NULL,
    start_at TIME (0) NOT NULL,
    end_at TIME (0) NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (store_id) REFERENCES sales.stores (store_id)
);

data.title: Insert TIME Values
data.content: Inserts a row with time values for a store visit.
data.code:
INSERT INTO sales.visits (
    customer_name,
    phone,
    store_id,
    visit_on,
    start_at,
    end_at
)
VALUES (
    'John Doe',
    '(408)-993-3853',
    1,
    '2018-06-23',
    '09:10:00',
    '09:30:00'
);

data.title: Note
data.text: The TIME data type is not time zone-aware. For time zone support, use DATETIMEOFFSET.

`TIME(p)` stores a time of day with a configurable precision, but it has no date part, so subtracting two TIME values directly is not the way to measure a duration. Convert to `DATETIME2` timestamps when you need elapsed time.

data.title: Time of day vs. duration
data.content: The first two columns show stored time values; the third shows a duration computed from two timestamps.

data.title: When to use which type
data.text: Use `TIME` for opening hours or a daily schedule, `DATETIME2` for an instant in time, and compute and store a duration column when the difference matters repeatedly (for example, `elapsed_seconds` on a job history table).

data.title: TIME Key Points
points: TIME stores only the time of day (no date component).
Fractional seconds precision ranges from 0 to 7.
Use TIME when you only need to store times, not dates.
